mandatory_notarization_and_apostille_bun.issuing_entity: Korean Commercial Registration Office at the competent district court under the Supreme Court of Korea
mandatory_notarization_and_apostille_bun.authentication_path: Apostille route: Korean notary public certification followed by Ministry of Foreign Affairs Apostille for use only in Hague Apostille Convention states. Consular route: Korean notary public certification followed by MOFA confirmation and legalization by the relevant embassy or consulate for non-member states. The routes are mutually exclusive and must never be applied sequentially.

mandatory_notarization_and_apostille_bun.document_name: Certificate of Good Standing (Company Registration Detail Certificate)
mandatory_notarization_and_apostille_bun.issuing_entity: Korean Commercial Registration Office and applicable tax office
mandatory_notarization_and_apostille_bun.authentication_path: Apostille route: notarization and MOFA Apostille for Apostille Convention countries; for non-member states, notarization followed by MOFA legalization visa at the destination consulate. These two paths are separate and not cumulative.

mandatory_notarization_and_apostille_bun.document_name: Board Resolution appointing the incorporation agent and authorizing the Power of Attorney
mandatory_notarization_and_apostille_bun.issuing_entity: Board of shareholders or directors, notarized in Korea
mandatory_notarization_and_apostille_bun.authentication_path: Notary authentication, then either MOFA Apostille for member jurisdictions or consular legalization for non-member jurisdictions. Neither consular legalization nor apostille may be added to the other.

mandatory_notarization_and_apostille_bun.issuing_entity: Founding shareholders and notarial office in Korea
mandatory_notarization_and_apostille_bun.authentication_path: MOFA Apostille after notarization for Hague Convention member states; for non-Hague states, notarized Korean charter submitted to the consular section of the destination country for legalization. Apostille and consular legalization remain exclusive alternatives.

mandatory_notarization_and_apostille_bun.document_name: Bank Reference Letter from an authorized Korean bank confirming customer due diligence
mandatory_notarization_and_apostille_bun.issuing_entity: FSS-regulated commercial bank or licensed foreign bank branch in Korea
mandatory_notarization_and_apostille_bun.authentication_path: Bank-issued letter signed by a compliance officer, notarized, then MOFA Apostille for member states or MOFA certification plus destination consulate legalization for non-member states. The legalization path must be selected by destination-country membership alone.

ubo_and_aml_profiling.pep_and_sanctions_screening_protocols: Mandatory real-time screening must be run against the Korea Financial Intelligence Unit's designated list, the United Nations Security Council consolidated sanctions list, an OFAC SDN and sectoral sanctions list, the European Union consolidated financial sanctions list, and all Korean domestic financial sanctions designations. All direct shareholders, ultimate beneficial owners, directors, senior officers, authorized signatories, and primary media-buying vendors must be screened for PEP status, adverse media, terrorism financing, and other reputational risk. Any PEP match requires senior-management approval and enhanced continuous monitoring before incorporation.

statutory_name_clearance_protocol.registry_portal_name: Supreme Court of Korea Internet Registration Office (IRRO) company name clearance and commercial registration portal of the competent district court registry
statutory_name_clearance_protocol.language_and_transliteration_doctrine: Korean statutory corporate names must be expressed in Hangul; the registered Korean name is controlling. A parallel transliterated English trade name may be recorded but it cannot replace the Hangul legal name. The name must follow the four-tier statutory structure: (1) distinctive element, (2) business-purpose describing element, (3) the corporate form suffix Yuhan Hoesa, and (4) an optional registered English trade name. Transliteration must follow the standard Romanization system published by the Ministry of Culture, Sports and Tourism, and must not create confusion with existing registrations.
statutory_name_clearance_protocol.extension_and_rejection_appeal_sop: A written administrative appeal must be filed with the issuing registry court within 15 days of the rejection notice, under Articles 42 and 107 of the Commercial Registration Act and the Administrative Litigation Act. The appeal must identify the rejected name, state the legal grounds, and attach the corrected Name Clearance Application and proof of counsel. If the registry court denies the appeal or fails to act within 30 days, the applicant may file an immediate appeal to the High Court. A fresh name clearance request may also be filed through the IRRO after removing the cited defect. Korean counsel must supervise all submissions.

registered_office_and_commercial_substan.virtual_office_permissibility: A virtual office or commercial mailbox-only address is not acceptable as the registered office of a Yuhan Hoesa in South Korea. The Korean Commercial Act and the Value-Added Tax Act require an actual domestic business address capable of receiving physical mail, notices, and process. For the digital advertising and affiliate media-buying business, the National Tax Service and FSS-regulated banks will decline a virtual address because they require proof of a fixed place of business during KYB and VAT registration. Foreign payment rails such as Mercury, Wise and standard wire transfers routinely reject virtual-office addresses for mixed ad-tech business models. A physical office lease, even a shared-management office with a dedicated identifiability suite, is mandatory to maintain good standing.
registered_office_and_commercial_substan.physical_inspection_likelihood: Likelihood: High (30-45% within the first 12 months for a new Yuhan Hoesa engaged in media buying and advertising invoicing). Checklist: (1) valid lease agreement in the company name, (2) power and utility contracts, (3) physical or digital signage at the registered address, (4) employee equipment and business records, (5) corporate bank account opened with the same address, and (6) VAT invoice footage matching the registered business address. Municipal and national tax officers plus court registry inspectors conduct unannounced on-site inspections; any mismatch or hollow mailbox arrangement will produce suspension of business registration and administrative fines.

incorporation_legal_framework.governing_statute_and_sections: Commercial Act of the Republic of Korea (Act No. 1000, as amended), Section 5 Limited Liability Company (Articles 287-2 through 287-42); Commercial Registration Act and its Enforcement Decree; Corporate Income Tax Act; Value-Added Tax Act
incorporation_legal_framework.competent_registry_authority: Commercial Registration Division, Seoul Central District Court, Supreme Court of Korea
incorporation_legal_framework.statutory_filing_instrument: Articles of Incorporation (Jeong-gwan) and Corporate Registration Application under the Commercial Registration Act
incorporation_legal_framework.minimum_paid_up_capital_rule: No statutory minimum paid-up capital exists under the Commercial Act for a Yuhan Hoesa; however, the subscribed capital must be fully paid before registration and the deposit must be evidenced by a bank-issued certificate of paid-in capital. Because this is a private limited company with no public offering, no mandatory blocked escrow account applies under the Capital Market Act; instead, a designated bank account in the name of the intended company or attorney trust account holds the funds until registration is completed. The Company's Articles prescribe KRW 100,000,000 of initial capital, fully paid in cash by the founding members.
incorporation_legal_framework.pro_forma_first_board_resolution_en: OF THE LIMITED LIABILITY COMPANY (YUHAN HOESA) KR_YUHANGHOESA. UNANIMOUS WRITTEN RESOLUTION OF THE FOUNDING DIRECTORS IN LIEU OF THE FIRST BOARD MEETING. The undersigned, being the founding directors of Yuhan Hoesa, a limited liability company organized under the Commercial Act of the Republic of Korea, hereby adopt the following resolutions in writing as permitted by the Articles of Incorporation and applicable law. All terms used herein shall have the meanings ascribed in the Articles of Incorporation. WHEREAS, the Company has been formed for the purpose of pursuing digital advertising media arbitrage and affiliate lead-generation activities classified under ISIC 7310 / NAICS 541810; and WHEREAS, Article 2 of the Articles of Incorporation fixes the registered office at 5th Floor, 17 Teheran-ro 4-gil, Gangnam-gu, Seoul 06132, Republic of Korea; and WHEREAS, the total initial capital contribution subscribed by the founding members is one hundred million Korean Won (KRW 100,000,000), divided into ten thousand (10,000) unit membership interests (deunpo) each with a par value of ten thousand Korean Won (KRW 10,000), all of which have been fully paid in cash. NOW THEREFORE, BE IT RESOLVED AS FOLLOWS: 1. The capital subscription schedule and the actual receipt of KRW 100,000,000 be, and hereby is, ratified and confirmed; each founding member shall be registered in the member register as the lawful owner of the corresponding membership interests free and clear of all encumbrances. 2. The registered office located at the address set forth in the Recitals above is adopted as the statutory registered office and principal place of business of the Company, and the corporate seal imprint (Gamdo) is directed to be affixed on all registration and banking instruments as instructed before effectuating the registration application. 3. Shinhan Bank, specifically the Gangnam Station Corporate Business Center, be and hereby is designated as the primary banking institution; the managing director is authorized to open corporate operating accounts, sign banking and treasury management mandates, and to receive, disburse, and manage Company funds. Further, any two of the authorized signatories are required to execute any transaction exceeding fifty million Korean Won (KRW 50,000,000). 4. Park Min-jae shall serve as the managing director (sadae-ri) responsible for daily operations, and Lee Ji-woo shall serve as the director of compliance and finance; both shall have statutory authority to represent the Company within the scope of the Articles. 5. Kim and Cho Certified Public Accountants is engaged to perform the statutory external audit for the first fiscal year and to prepare the annual tax filings under the Corporate Tax Act. 6. The managing director, together with the registered statutory agent, is directed to execute and file the corporation registration application with Seoul Central District Court Registration Division, complete the business registration with the Gangnam District Tax Office, and take all ancillary actions necessary to achieve legal existence and operational good standing of the Company. RESOLVED FURTHER, that any officer or authorized attorney-in-fact be empowered to appear before notaries, courts, administrative agencies, and banks as required to execute, swear, and submit any document necessary to the formation. This Written Resolution is effective as of 1 July 2025, without the necessity of a physical meeting, and shall be filed in the corporate minute book.

step_by_step_formation_sop.step_name: Name Availability Review, Article Drafting, and Notarization
step_by_step_formation_sop.competent_authority: Commercial Registration Information System (Supreme Court of Korea) and local Korean notary public
step_by_step_formation_sop.detailed_action_protocol: Conduct a preliminary name availability review on the Commercial Registration Information System maintained by the Korean Supreme Court, testing the proposed Korean legal name and a parallel English alias; then instruct a duly licensed notary public to authenticate the signatures of all founding members on the Articles of Incorporation. The notary must declare that each member consented to the capital contribution and appointment of the managing director. After notarization, the notary prepares the certified copy of the Articles, together with a certificate of authentication that will accompany the registration application. All identifications must be valid passports or alien registration cards and apostilled where required.
required_dossiers: Articles of Incorporation signed by all founding members
Power of attorney to local incorporating attorney
Passports or alien registration cards of all directors
step_by_step_formation_sop.adverse_action_remedies: If the name search returns a conflict and cannot be reserved, the incorporator will immediately file an amended Articles draft with up to three alternate names. Any corrective request from the notary regarding the Articles content triggers a reverify-and-resubmit cycle within three business days. If the search is suspended due to pending registrations, applicant may wait for 72 hours and refile with a disclaimer of similarity, or petition the registry for a name-confirmatory letter.

step_by_step_formation_sop.step_name: Capital Subscription and Bank Deposit Verification
step_by_step_formation_sop.competent_authority: Shinhan Bank - Gangnam Station Corporate Business Center; certified public accountant for contribution verification
step_by_step_formation_sop.detailed_action_protocol: After the Articles are notarized, open a corporate provisional account or attorney trust account under the exact intended company name, and instruct each member to wire their capital contribution with remitter identification fully matching the member name in the Articles. Once all installments arrive, request the bank to issue a Certificate of Paid-in Capital (or deposit balance certificate) containing the account holder, aggregate amount, and date, dated within three months of filing. The certificate is then attached to the registration application. If any member contributes in kind, such as software licenses or marketing contracts, obtain a separate appraisal and contribution audit from a licensed certified public accountant.
required_dossiers: Bank account statement for provisional account
In-kind contribution audit report if applicable
step_by_step_formation_sop.adverse_action_remedies: If the bank refuses issuance due to a name mismatch, the company executes an amendment to the Articles or a deed of re-designation and resubmits. If the deposit certificate is queried by the registry, the bank must issue a supplementary confirmation with the full payment trace and the managing director's identity. Any missing item in the bank dossier is cured by filing an additional statement of account and a sworn declaration from the managing director.

step_by_step_formation_sop.competent_authority: Commercial Registration Division, Seoul Central District Court, Supreme Court of Korea
step_by_step_formation_sop.detailed_action_protocol: Within sixty calendar days after the members' approval, prepare and submit the corporate registration application using the Official Registration Form of the Commercial Registration Act. Attach the notarized original Articles, the paid-in capital certificate, the directors' appointment consent, and the proof of parent entity incorporation if applicable. Pay the registration fee and any notarial stamp in cash or by legal fee stamp at the registry window. The presiding registration registrar reviews the statutory particulars and will issue a certified copy of registration after a successful substantive and formal check. The registry maintains an online service to verify the corporate existence. The corporate seal imprint must be submitted with the application and the authenticity of the representative is verified.
required_dossiers: Apostilled parent company registration if foreign member
step_by_step_formation_sop.adverse_action_remedies: If the registration is queried or suspended for correction, the court issues a written corrigendum stating missing documents or inconsistent clauses. The registrant must cure within two weeks, failing which the application is deemed dismissed; an administrative appeal to the Seoul High Court is available. In practice, the attorney refiles with a formal response and additional evidence within five business days to avoid lapse.

step_by_step_formation_sop.step_name: Business Registration, Tax Identification, and Social Insurance Enrollment
step_by_step_formation_sop.competent_authority: Gangnam District Tax Office (National Tax Service); National Pension Service; National Health Insurance Service; Korea Workers' Compensation and Employment Insurance Service
step_by_step_formation_sop.detailed_action_protocol: Using the commercial registration certificate obtained from the court registry, file an initial business registration return with the National Tax Service within twenty days of business commencement. The NTS will attach a business registration certificate, issue a corporate tax ID and VAT registration, and require the issuance of electronic tax invoices. In parallel, register all directors and employees with the four social insurance systems. Failure to file business registration results in additional penalties and possible blacklisting from overdue VAT refunds. The tax office will also issue a certificate of business registration required to open the final corporate bank account.
required_dossiers: Managing director identity and resident registration certificate
step_by_step_formation_sop.adverse_action_remedies: If the tax office issues a notice of nonrevenue or missing document, the registered agent submits an explanation and corrected form within seven days. If any social insurance registration is refused, the focal authority must issue a written rejection; the company appeals to the Central Administrative Appeals Commission, but taxable operations may commence while the appeal is pending.

industry_physical_and_environmental_lice.competent_industrial_authority: Not Applicable - Pure digital advertising media buying and affiliate marketing firm with no physical manufacturing, chemical, assembly, or warehousing operations.
industry_physical_and_environmental_lice.operating_license_title: Not Applicable - No operating permit required under Korean industrial licensing statutes for ISIC 7310 / NAICS 541810 activities.

environmental_impact_assessment_eia.agency_name: Not Applicable - Pure digital advertising and media buying business; no physical construction or manufacturing activities under the Environmental Impact Assessment Act.
environmental_impact_assessment_eia.classification_tier: Exempt - Not an EIA-subject business based on ISIC 7310 / NAICS 541810 classifications.
environmental_impact_assessment_eia.discharge_and_emissions_standards: Not Applicable - zero regulated discharge of wastewater, VOCs, or hazardous waste from the registered office; no point-source emission.

industry_physical_and_environmental_lice.civil_defense_and_occupational_clearance: Not Applicable - The Company leases a Class 1 office suite and does not own or operate a warehouse, chemical plant, or industrial facility. The building owner remains responsible for the fire-safety certification under the Fire Prevention, Installation, Maintenance and Safety Control Act. The Company will, however, implement a general occupational safety and health policy under the Occupational Safety and Health Act, covering office ergonomics, emergency evacuation drills, and electrical equipment safety; no separate Civil Defense fire permit is required.

national_tax_registration_infrastructure.competent_tax_authority: National Tax Service (NTS) of South Korea; online portal is Home Tax Service (Hometax) at hometax.go.kr
national_tax_registration_infrastructure.tax_id_procurement_sop: A foreign non-resident entity seeking a Korean Corporate Taxpayer Identification Number must first determine whether it has a domestic place of business (fixed place of business) under Article 119 of the Income Tax Act or a permanent establishment under Article 2 of the Corporation Tax Act. If the entity is engaged in the supply of digital advertising media buying and affiliate lead generation services through a Korean intermediary, a server, or a dependent agent in Korea, registration with the NTS is required. The procedure is: (1) Prepare the Certificate of Incorporation, Articles of Association, and a notarized power of attorney appointing a domestic tax representative if the foreign entity has no domestic place of business; (2) file an application for corporate registration using the Corporate Taxpayer Registration Application Form at the competent district tax office having jurisdiction over the place of business, or electronically via Hometax; (3) obtain the Business Registration Certificate (Business Registration Number) for corporate income tax purposes; (4) separately apply for a VAT Business Registration Number when the entity is registered or required to register for VAT; (5) verify whether simplified registration for foreign corporations without a domestic place of business applies for VAT; (6) register for mandatory electronic tax invoice issuance; (7) upon completion, the NTS issues the taxpayer identification number, which is the same as the Business Registration Number for corporate tax and VAT purposes.
national_tax_registration_infrastructure.statutory_election_mechanisms: None for a Yuhan Hoesa (LLC). Korean domestic companies are taxed at entity level under the Corporation Tax Act and cannot elect pass-through treatment. No check-the-box election exists. Hybrid mismatch elections under OECD BEPS Action 2 are not administrative elections available to a domestic entity; only treaty-based permanent establishment determinations may vary by applicable tax treaty.

indirect_taxation_nexus_and_rules.indirect_tax_system_name: Value Added Tax (VAT) under the Value-Added Tax Act of South Korea
indirect_taxation_nexus_and_rules.statutory_registration_threshold_local_c: For corporations, including a Yuhan Hoesa LLC, VAT registration is mandatory from the start of business regardless of turnover; there is no minimum threshold. For individuals and sole proprietors, mandatory registration triggers when taxable turnover in the prior calendar year exceeds KRW 80,000,000.
indirect_taxation_nexus_and_rules.electronic_invoicing_and_clearance_manda: All VAT-registered taxpayers must issue electronic tax invoices (e-Tax Invoices) under Article 32 of the VAT Act for B2B transactions. Issuance must be transmitted to the NTS through Hometax or an approved e-invoice service provider in XML format. Since 1 July 2024, the mandatory electronic tax invoice system applies fully, and the NTS operates a real-time transmission and validation framework requiring API-based or machine-to-machine integration for high-risk B2B transactions. VAT returns are filed quarterly for corporations, with electronic filing mandatory. Anti-fraud controls include assigned electronic serial numbers, buyer VAT number verification, and 24-hour validation through the NTS tax invoice status transmission service. Non-compliance triggers penalties under Article 32-5 of the VAT Act and Article 125-1 of the Framework Act on National Taxes.

export_zero_rating_and_refund_substantia.zero_rating_eligibility: Zero-rated VAT treatment applies to the export of goods physically exported under customs declaration and to the supply of services and digital services to non-resident recipients for use wholly outside Korea, including digital advertising, affiliate marketing, and lead generation services supplied by a Korean entity to a foreign business recipient. Eligibility requires proof that the recipient is a non-resident without a domestic place of business in Korea, the place of supply is outside Korea, the contract and invoices designate offshore supply, and the services are not rendered to Korean consumers. Advertising services on exported goods and services supplied to foreign clients may also qualify under Article 21 of the VAT Act and the VAT Act Enforcement Decree. In all cases the exporter must hold full documentation substantiating the foreign destination and collection of proceeds.
mandatory_customs_documentation_bundle: Customs Export Declaration filed through the Korea Customs Service UNI-PASS system
Bill of Lading (B/L), Air Waybill (AWB), or comparable shipment receipt
Inward Remittance Certificate (FIRC) issued by a Korean foreign-exchange bank, or SWIFT/MT103 wire confirmation evidencing foreign exchange repatriation
Commercial invoice stating the export price and the 0% VAT treatment
Copy of the export contract with the overseas buyer, including Incoterms and place-of-supply terms
Korean customs export performance confirmation (Export Performance Certificate)

For services: zero-rated electronic tax invoice referencing the foreign recipient's VAT/GST identification number, together with the service contract and evidence that the recipient is a non-resident business and all benefit is derived outside Korea
Foreign exchange transaction reporting data from the Foreign Exchange Information System (FXIS) where applicable
export_zero_rating_and_refund_substantia.audit_scrutiny_and_clawback_penalties: If the documented export is not substantiated by customs declarations, actual cross-border movement of goods, or verifiable foreign exchange repatriation within the statutory period, the NTS may reverse the zero-rating and assess 10% VAT on the supply, plus penalties of up to 40% of the unpaid tax for negligent underreporting or intentional misstatement, 10% for underdeclared tax, and monthly late-payment interest of 0.022% per day from the original due date. Fictitious or fraudulent export invoices can trigger criminal prosecution under the Punishment of Tax Evaders Act, with imprisonment up to 2 years or fines up to KRW 50,000,000. Retroactive clawbacks may include all input VAT credits claimed in connection with the false export, and the statute of limitations extends to 3 years generally, or 5 years for intentional evasion.

fx_control_regime_and_central_bank_regul.central_bank_authority: The Bank of Korea (BOK), with delegated authority from the Ministry of Strategy and Finance (MOSF), is the central foreign-exchange authority under the Foreign Exchange Transactions Act of the Republic of Korea; actual execution and supervision are carried out through authorized foreign exchange banks.
fx_control_regime_and_central_bank_regul.currency_convertibility_assessment: South Korea maintains a liberal current-account system under the Foreign Exchange Transactions Act, but the Korean won is not an offshore freely deliverable currency; KRW convertibility is provided exclusively through authorized foreign exchange banks integrated with the Bank of Korea settlement system. Current-account receipts and payments for trade, service fees, and profit remittances are generally permitted without prior approval, while capital-account transactions, including FDI share purchases and non-resident borrowing, are subject to reporting or approval. A Yuhan Hoesa receiving inbound equity must ensure that every dollar is remitted with a correct foreign-investment report; otherwise the foreign exchange bank will reject the credit or the Bank of Korea will issue a correction order. Remittance of dividends is supervised: the bank will require audited financial statements, evidence of corporate tax payment and withholding, and a shareholder resolution. The practical hurdle is documentary exactness, not convertibility itself. Overseas banks do not hold domestic KRW clearing accounts, and offshore KRW trading is largely an NDF market outside the legal onshore settlement perimeter. Therefore the treasury blueprint must keep the onshore KRW liquidity ring inside regulated banks and route every convertible flow through declared business purposes with full transactional provenance.
fx_control_regime_and_central_bank_regul.export_proceeds_surrender_rules: Under the Foreign Exchange Transactions Act and its Enforcement Regulations, Korea imposes no mandatory cash surrender percentage on export proceeds. Exporters must settle export-related foreign currency receipts through an authorized foreign exchange bank and are required to bring the proceeds onshore within 90 days from export clearance; an extension to 180 days may be granted by the bank if the exporter submits a collection plan and proves an acceptable payment risk profile. The proceeds may be credited to a foreign currency account or converted into KRW at the bank's market rate. Failure to repatriate on time or to file the required extension report triggers administrative reporting to the Ministry of Strategy and Finance and can result in penalties or loss of treasury accommodation.

tier1_domestic_commercial_banks.account_class: FDI Capital Escrow Account and Basic Operational KRW/USD Currency Account
FDI Capital Escrow Account and Basic Operational KRW/USD Currency Account
FDI Capital Escrow Account and Basic Operational KRW/USD Currency Account

corporate_banking_onboarding_blueprint.fintech_emi_cross_border_viability: Low. Under the Electronic Financial Transactions Act and the Foreign Exchange Transactions Act, non-bank fintech EMIs such as Wise are not licensed to open domestic KRW transaction accounts for regulated corporate entities or to act as the primary foreign-exchange settlement counterparty without a foreign-exchange business license from the Bank of Korea and authorization from the Financial Services Commission. A Yuhan Hoesa registered in the Republic of Korea must maintain its FDI capital escrow and core operating liquidity with an authorized domestic Tier-1 bank. Digital EMI rails may only be used as supplemental channels for incidental non-KRW payments to overseas vendors after the main treasury spine is established at a licensed bank, and no equity injection or dividend repatriation may pass through such EMIs.
corporate_banking_onboarding_blueprint.physical_presence_and_kyc_interview_mand: Korean Tier-1 banks require a physical director interview for the initial corporate account opening under most enhanced due diligence cases. Non-resident statutory directors may open through a power of attorney granted to a domestic signatory, provided the foreign director completes consular notarization and a verified video eKYC call; however, for cross-border media buying and affiliate networks, most banks still demand at least one face-to-face interview in-branch with the authorized economic owner, the beneficial owner, or the resident officer. Remote consular proxy opening is not universally accepted and remains at the bank's discretion; banks may require a visit to a designated overseas branch of the same banking group for identity verification before activation of the account.

critical_aml_kyc_blockers_and_defense.trigger_point: The beneficial owner and statutory director are not an obvious match for the digital advertising control function, raising CDD concerns over nominee structures and hidden principals.
critical_aml_kyc_blockers_and_defense.evidentiary_defense_dossier: Valid passport or national ID, Alien Registration Card, ultimate beneficial owner declaration, corporate registry extracts proving a transparent ownership chain, certificate of incumbency, director resolution appointing the domestic signatory, and signed declaration confirming no adverse media, sanctions exposure, or politically exposed person status without disclosure.

critical_aml_kyc_blockers_and_defense.trigger_point: Outbound payments to affiliate networks and offshore media agency accounts lack a physical goods trail and create a high layering risk, typical of performance media buying where the ultimate beneficiary is unclear.
critical_aml_kyc_blockers_and_defense.evidentiary_defense_dossier: Executed affiliate contracts and publisher insertion orders, audited campaign performance reports, platform invoices from providers such as Google Ads and Meta, the affiliate network's KYC onboarding documents, external payment register, and a projected clearing schedule with transaction thresholds and monthly reconciliation.

critical_aml_kyc_blockers_and_defense.trigger_point: Frequent multi-currency conversions with unregistered FX split positions may be characterized as unlawful foreign-exchange business or speculative treasury activity rather than genuine commercial hedging.
critical_aml_kyc_blockers_and_defense.evidentiary_defense_dossier: Confirmed foreign-exchange transaction slips with the authorized bank, monthly reconciliation of inbound USD and outbound KRW payments, statutory purpose codes aligned to advertising and licensing fees, and if any NDF or forward is used, the trade confirmation, underlying exposure documents, and a board-approved treasury policy restricting derivatives to hedging.

cross_border_liquidity_and_clearing_rail.inbound_capital_injection_routing: All inbound equity for the Yuhan Hoesa must be routed via SWIFT MT103 from the shareholder's account directly to the FDI capital escrow account opened at an authorized foreign exchange bank. The remittance reason must use a capital-account foreign-exchange purpose code for foreign direct investment, with the FDI report completed and submitted to the bank before the credit is posted. After the credit clears, the bank verifies the capital against the reported amount, issues capital verification and foreign investor registration documents, and releases the funds to the entity's operational KRW account. The bank then files the transaction electronically through the Foreign Exchange Information System. The treasury must never allow the equity to be pre-funded through third-party payment wallets, digital EMIs, or personal accounts.
cross_border_liquidity_and_clearing_rail.outbound_trade_disbursements: Operational disbursements should flow through the single authorized foreign exchange bank. SWIFT MT103 is the default rail for affiliate commissions, media agency invoices, and recurring cross-border service fees, with payment metadata showing beneficiary bank, exact legal entity beneficiary, and invoice reference. For larger media procurement contracts with recognized vendors, commercial letters of credit or documentary collections may be used where the invoice is contractually supported and the service delivery schedule is specific. Domestic KRW payments to Korean publishers, influencers, and suppliers must clear through BOK-Wire+ or domestic OTC bank transfer rails and be reported as current-account payments. Payments to sanctioned jurisdictions or to any unverified beneficiary must be systemically blocked.
permissible_fx_hedging_instruments: Onshore KRW/USD FX forward contracts up to 100% of the underlying trade, affiliate receivables, or media payables, with supporting invoices and contracts, executed through an authorized foreign exchange bank
FX options combined with forward structures for cash-flow smoothing, but only with real commercial exposure and no embedded leverage beyond the underlying position

Non-deliverable forwards (NDFs) for companies with an offshore treasury center or matching KRW trade cash flows, booked through the authorized bank's offshore desk; speculative onshore NDF positions are prohibited

Cross-currency swaps permitted where a real foreign capital loan or receivable exists and the swap is aligned with the maturity and amount of the underlying capital transaction, with no net open speculative position

annual_compliance_calendar_matrix.statutory_deliverable: Corporate Income Tax Base and Tax Amount Return (with certified or internally prepared financial statements attached) and Local Corporate Income Tax Surtax Return
annual_compliance_calendar_matrix.receiving_authority: National Tax Service (NTS) of South Korea, filed through the Home Tax Service e-filing portal; the collected surtax is remitted by the NTS to the applicable si/gun/gu local government
annual_compliance_calendar_matrix.statutory_deadline_window: Within three months after the end of the fiscal year; for a calendar-year Yuhan Hoesa, by March 31. An extension of up to one month may be available for entities with total assets exceeding KRW 10 billion if the extension is applied for before the original due date.
annual_compliance_calendar_matrix.delinquency_sanctions: Late or non-filing attracts an additional tax equal to 20% of the tax paid (40% in fraudulent cases); under-declaration attracts an additional 10% (40% if fraudulent); unpaid taxes accrue overdue interest at 0.025% per day; persistent non-filing and delinquency can trigger NTS tax seizure, closure of the business registration, director liability, and ultimately administrative forced deregistration via court-ordered dissolution.

annual_compliance_calendar_matrix.statutory_deliverable: Annual Statistical Fixture of Financial Statements and Independent Auditor's Report (only if the mandatory statutory audit threshold is met; otherwise not filed with the Financial Supervisory Service)
annual_compliance_calendar_matrix.receiving_authority: Financial Supervisory Service (FSS) of South Korea and its Electronic Disclosure System (DART); a copy is also attached to the NTS corporate income tax return
annual_compliance_calendar_matrix.statutory_deadline_window: The financial statements must be approved by the annual general meeting of members within six months of the fiscal year end; the audited financial statements must be filed with the DART/FSS within 14 days after such approval, and in all cases by the statutory extended corporate tax return due date where required.
annual_compliance_calendar_matrix.delinquency_sanctions: Failure to receive a close to the external audit mandatorily required under the Act on External Audit of Stock Companies results in administrative penalties up to KRW 30 million and may lead to refusal by the NTS to accept the corporate tax return; persistent failure can trigger a forced audit ordered by the Financial Services Commission, public disclosure of violations, and personal liability of directors for resulting corporate tax losses.

annual_compliance_calendar_matrix.receiving_authority: National Tax Service (NTS) of South Korea
annual_compliance_calendar_matrix.statutory_deadline_window: First half-year (January 1 to June 30) return is due by July 25; second half-year (July 1 to December 31) return is due by January 25 of the following year.
annual_compliance_calendar_matrix.delinquency_sanctions: Late payment interest accrues at 0.025% per day; failure to file carries an additional tax of 10% of the tax payable; late payment carries an additional 10%; understated output tax on taxable supplies may attract a 10% additional assessment, and intentional miscalculation can be escalated to criminal tax evasion penalties; persistent non-filing exposes the entity and its representative to tax seizures and administrative deregistration actions.

annual_compliance_calendar_matrix.statutory_deliverable: Foreign Investment Annual Status Report (applicable only when the Yuhan Hoesa is classified as a foreign-invested company under the Foreign Investment Promotion Act)
annual_compliance_calendar_matrix.receiving_authority: Ministry of Trade, Industry and Energy (MOTIE), administered by KOTRA and the registered foreign exchange bank in charge of the foreign investment
annual_compliance_calendar_matrix.statutory_deadline_window: Within 30 days after the end of each fiscal year, the foreign-invested company must submit the annual business status report on the immediately preceding fiscal year; from the filing of certificates of adoption of the completed fiscal year performance data.
annual_compliance_calendar_matrix.delinquency_sanctions: Failure to file or filing false information may expose the foreign investor and the Korean entity to administrative fines up to KRW 3 million; the foreign investment designation may be revoked, and exchange-control privileges such as dividend remittance guarantees may be suspended; the entity may also be subjected to enhanced AML/CFT review by custodian financial institutions.

statutory_audit_and_accounting_mandate.compulsory_audit_thresholds: Under the Republic of Korea's Act on External Audit of Stock Companies and its Presidential Enforcement Decree, a Yuhan Hoesa is legally required to appoint an independent certified public accountant and undergo a statutory audit if, at the end of the immediately preceding fiscal year, total assets equal or exceed KRW 12 billion (approximately USD 8.9 million). The same statutory audit is also mandatory for a Yuhan Hoesa that is formed or continued as an entity subject to external audit by presidential decree, including any entity whose securities are listed or whose shares are traded on a Korean exchange, any entity that falls into special categories such as holding companies with material public interest, and any company that has been ordered by the Securities and Futures Commission to appoint an outside auditor due to failure of internal accounting control. In practice, banks and foreign affiliates may also require a certified audit even below the statutory threshold if the financial report is used for credit extension, overseas remittance, or merger consolidation.
statutory_audit_and_accounting_mandate.governing_accounting_framework: K-IFRS (Korean International Financial Reporting Standards) is mandatory for listed companies and certain large non-public companies; a non-listed Yuhan Hoesa subject to external audit may apply K-GAAP (Korean Generally Accepted Accounting Principles) for non-public companies; a small and medium-scale Yuhan Hoesa that does not qualify as a listed or large company may adopt the Korean SMEs Accounting Standards (K-SMEAS) provided it meets the eligibility criteria of the enforcement decree. The statutory audit opinion itself must be issued under the Korean Auditing Standards (KSA) established by the Korean Institute of Certified Public Accountants and referenced in the Act on External Audit of Stock Companies. Accounting records, vouchers, and statutory ledgers must be retained for at least seven years, and for VAT-related records the retention period is also aligned to the Commercial Act and the Framework Act on National Taxes.

corporate_registers_and_ubo_annual_confi.ubo_annual_confirmation_protocol: South Korea does not maintain a single publicly searchable annual UBO filing for non-listed limited liability companies. Under the Korean Commercial Act, a Yuhan Hoesa must keep a register of members and record every transfer of an equity interest; the transfer becomes effective against the company and third parties only upon written entry in the register of members, including the name, address, and role of the new member. If the Yuhan Hoesa is a foreign-invested company, the foreign investor and the company must report any change in ownership interest, voting rights, share capital, or business purpose to the designated foreign exchange bank and KOTRA/MOTIE within 30 days of the change, and any outward remittance of dividend or liquidation proceeds is conditioned on correct UBO and investment reporting. For AML/CFT purposes under the Act on Reporting and Using Specified Financial Transaction Information, the company must provide accurate beneficial ownership information to its service bank whenever an account is opened or updated, and the bank must be notified within a reasonable 30-day window of any material beneficial ownership shift. There is no separate fee for UBO filing in the ordinary course for the standalone Yuhan Hoesa unless a court registration of share transfer or capital change is required, in which case registration court fees apply.
mandatory_on_site_statutory_registers: Register of Charges/Mortgages and Pledges on Equity Interests
Minute Book containing minutes of members' meetings and directors' meetings

recurring_annual_maintenance_budget_usd.registered_office_or_agent_market_range_: USD 350 - USD 1,500 per year in the greater Seoul area, depending on serviced office quality, mail handling, registered agent services, and compliance oversight; smaller regional offices may be USD 250 - USD 900 per year
recurring_annual_maintenance_budget_usd.statutory_audit_estimated_fee_usd: USD 5,000 - USD 18,000 per year if the mandatory external audit threshold is triggered; USD 2,500 - USD 6,000 per year for an optional agreed-upon procedures review or internal control review when no statutory audit is required

corporate_income_tax_regime.statutory_headline_rate: 24% national corporate income tax on taxable income above KRW 300 billion, plus a 10% local income tax surtax, producing an aggregate headline rate of 26.4%; lower resident brackets are 9% up to KRW 200 million, 19% up to KRW 20 billion, and 21% up to KRW 300 billion.
corporate_income_tax_regime.effective_tax_rate_incentives: Foreign-invested enterprises in Free Economic Zones or Foreign Investment Zones may receive a 5-year 100% corporate tax reduction followed by a 2-year 50% reduction under the Restriction of Special Taxation Act Articles 121.2 and 121.4; R&D tax credits up to 20-30% of qualifying expenditure under Article 10; special SME and venture company rate reductions; no separate patent box exists, but qualifying technology transfer income is taxed at reduced or deferred rates.

tax_return_filing_anatomy.form_identifier_and_portal: Corporate Income Tax Return (Corporate Tax Act Form Group 12-B) filed electronically through the National Tax Service HomeTax web portal at hometax.go.kr, with supporting schedules for tax base adjustments and transfer-pricing disclosures.
tax_return_filing_anatomy.reporting_frequency: Annual final filing, with an interim prepayment filing generally required for the first six months of the fiscal year.
tax_return_filing_anatomy.statutory_deadline_rule: The annual return must be filed within three months after the fiscal year-end; for a calendar-year entity the deadline is March 31 of the following year.

field_by_field_filling_dissection.line_or_box_code: Section 1, Box 01 - Fiscal Year and Entity Status
field_by_field_filling_dissection.entry_description: Identifies the tax period, corporate registration number, legal form as a Yuhan Hoesa limited company, and the place of effective management.
field_by_field_filling_dissection.non_resident_entry_guidance: If foreign shareholders control the LLC but Korean directors exercise strategic, operational, and financial control, declare resident domestic corporation status and report worldwide income; a non-resident-owned entity that is a mere nominee must disclose the actual owner to avoid recharacterization.

field_by_field_filling_dissection.entry_description: Totals revenue from affiliate media buying, advertiser rebates, performance commissions, lead generation fees, and demand-side platform margins, stated net of value-added tax.
field_by_field_filling_dissection.non_resident_entry_guidance: A non-resident entity without a Korean permanent establishment reports only Korean-source income for final withholding purposes; a Korean-resident LLC must report all worldwide gross revenue and separately disclose related-party revenue to support arm's-length pricing.

field_by_field_filling_dissection.entry_description: Records book-tax differences, non-deductible expenses, tax-exempt income, depreciation recapture, and intercompany fee true-ups.
field_by_field_filling_dissection.non_resident_entry_guidance: Add back fees paid to related offshore media-buying shells unless supported by OECD-compliant benchmarking, actual services, and economic substance; disallow payments to tax-haven affiliates where no personnel, decision-making, or risk-bearing capacity exists in the invoice counterparty.

field_by_field_filling_dissection.entry_description: Deducts eligible prior-year net operating losses within the statutory carryforward period.
field_by_field_filling_dissection.non_resident_entry_guidance: A Korean-resident LLC may carry forward qualifying losses for up to 15 fiscal years; a non-resident corporation's Korean branch may offset losses only against future Korean branch profits, and loss carryforward may be denied on a change of ownership made for tax avoidance.

field_by_field_filling_dissection.line_or_box_code: Section 5, Box 05 - Tax Base, Rate Calculation, and Local Surtax
field_by_field_filling_dissection.entry_description: Applies the resident progressive corporate tax rates to the taxable income base and adds the 10% local income tax surtax.
field_by_field_filling_dissection.non_resident_entry_guidance: Compute using the resident scales: 9% up to KRW 200 million, 19% up to KRW 20 billion, 21% up to KRW 300 billion, and 24% above KRW 300 billion; a non-resident without a Korean permanent establishment is generally outside this calculation and instead suffers final withholding under Corporate Tax Act Article 98.

field_by_field_filling_dissection.line_or_box_code: Section 6, Box 06 - Foreign Tax Credit and Net Tax Payable
field_by_field_filling_dissection.entry_description: Claims foreign tax credits, dividend-received deductions, interim prepayments, and any DTA-reduced withholding credits to compute net corporate tax payable.
field_by_field_filling_dissection.non_resident_entry_guidance: Attach a tax residency certificate and a treaty-benefits schedule for each outbound dividend, interest, or royalty payment; substantiate beneficial ownership and no-conduit facts before applying a reduced DTA rate; late DTA relief is handled by refund claim within the statutory five-year window and not by unilateral reduction of statutory withholding without authority.

tax_return_filing_anatomy.failure_penalties: Late filing and underreporting are assessed under Corporate Tax Act Articles 47-2 and 47-3: 10% additional tax for negligent underpayment, 20% for dishonest underreporting or non-filing, and 40% for fraudulent non-filing or omission; unpaid tax continues to accrue a daily delinquency surcharge, and criminal prosecution under the Punishment of Tax Evaders Act can lead to imprisonment up to 5 years or a fine up to ten times the tax evaded; directors may face departure restrictions where intentional evasion exceeds the National Tax Service blacklisting threshold.

profit_repatriation_and_withholding_tax.statutory_dividend_wht_rate: 22% on gross outbound dividends (20% corporate income tax withholding plus 2% local income tax surtax), subject to reduction under an applicable bilateral double tax treaty, commonly to 5% or 10% for a qualified substantial corporate shareholder.
profit_repatriation_and_withholding_tax.treaty_relief_application_protocol: To invoke DTA relief, the non-resident recipient must obtain a Tax Residency Certificate from the treaty country, provide it to the Korean withholding agent or tax office before or at the time of payment, complete the applicable treaty-benefit and beneficial ownership forms, and substantiate that it is not an intermediary, back-to-back, or substance-less conduit; the Korean payer must maintain the TRC, LOB analysis, shareholder ownership proof, and payment Vouchers for audit; if relief was not applied in time, the recipient may file a refund application with the National Tax Service within five years.
profit_repatriation_and_withholding_tax.cross_border_royalty_and_interest_wht: Statutory withholding on Korean-source royalties and interest is 22% (20% corporate income tax plus 2% local surtax); DTA rates frequently reduce interest to 10-15% and royalties to 10%, depending on the treaty, and require the same TRC and beneficial ownership evidence as dividend relief, with additional limitations for excessive debt under Korea's thin capitalization rules.

transfer_pricing_and_economic_substance.tp_documentation_threshold_local_currenc: Local File becomes mandatory when aggregate cross-border related-party transactions reach KRW 10 billion during the fiscal year; Master File may be required when annual revenue reaches KRW 100 billion and related-party transactions exceed KRW 10 billion; transfer-pricing disclosure is filed with the annual corporate tax return and must be submitted on request within a statutory time limit.
transfer_pricing_and_economic_substance.economic_substance_doctrine: Korea applies a substance-over-form doctrine through Corporate Tax Act Article 170 and International Tax Adjustment Act Article 4; for an affiliate media-buying entity, the Core Income-Generating Activities must be performed by Korean personnel, including contract negotiation, media purchasing decisions, risk assumption, and oversight of affiliate networks; a paper LLC that merely invoices commissions while actual functions remain with shareholders or foreign affiliates will have its transactions recharacterized, profit reallocated, and treaty benefits denied.

fatal_compliance_red_flags_and_liabiliti.triggering_act: The Korean Yuhan Hoesa earns affiliate media-buying revenue from Korean advertisers and lead-generation networks but omits the revenue from the Corporate Tax Return and diverts receipts to related foreign bank accounts through nominee contracts.
fatal_compliance_red_flags_and_liabiliti.statutory_sanction: Corporate Tax Act Articles 47-2 and 47-3 impose additional taxes of 10% to 40% of the underreported or unreported tax, and Article 3 of the Punishment of Tax Evaders Act imposes imprisonment up to 5 years or a fine up to ten times the evaded tax, or both.
fatal_compliance_red_flags_and_liabiliti.personal_liability_of_directors: Under National Tax Collection Act Article 311, the representative director becomes a secondary taxpayer when the company's assets are insufficient because of intentional evasion; courts may pierce the corporate veil where the LLC is a mere instrumentality, and directors face civil restitution for company losses under Commercial Act Article 399, travel bans, asset attachment, and individual criminal liability including imprisonment.

fatal_compliance_red_flags_and_liabiliti.infraction_category: Shell affiliate misuse and transfer pricing documentation failure
fatal_compliance_red_flags_and_liabiliti.triggering_act: The Korean LLC employs all media-buying specialists, holds advertiser contracts, and bears commercial risk in Seoul, but invoices commissions through a zero-employee foreign affiliate at a non-arm's-length markup and fails to prepare a Local File or Master File despite exceeding the KRW 10 billion related-party transaction threshold.
fatal_compliance_red_flags_and_liabiliti.statutory_sanction: The tax office may disregard the intermediary under International Tax Adjustment Act Article 4, reallocate profit to Korea, impose an additional tax on intercompany adjustments, deny deductions for the inflated fees, and apply Foreign Exchange Transactions Act penalties for illegal cross-border remittances.
fatal_compliance_red_flags_and_liabiliti.personal_liability_of_directors: Directors who signed offshore service agreements without real service substance can be held personally liable for restitution and secondary tax obligations; the representative director may be blacklisted, issued a departure ban, and charged with intentional documentation fraud under the Punishment of Tax Evaders Act and the Act on the Aggravated Punishment of Specific Economic Crimes.

fatal_compliance_red_flags_and_liabiliti.infraction_category: Anti-money laundering and cross-border payment concealment
fatal_compliance_red_flags_and_liabiliti.triggering_act: The company routes affiliate commissions through Wise, Mercury ACH, and third-party virtual accounts without performing customer due diligence on media suppliers, fails to file suspicious transaction reports, and conceals the ultimate beneficial owner of the Korean LLC.
fatal_compliance_red_flags_and_liabiliti.statutory_sanction: The Specific Financial Information Act imposes criminal liability for AML breaches, including imprisonment and statutory fines, and the Foreign Exchange Transactions Act Article 30 penalizes unrecorded outward remittances with fines and confiscation; AML penalties may be assessed on both the company and the directing officers.
fatal_compliance_red_flags_and_liabiliti.personal_liability_of_directors: Compliance officers and directors who knowingly direct concealed payment flows are personally criminally liable for violations, individual bank accounts may be frozen, travel bans are imposed during investigation, and civil asset restitution is available to aggrieved counterparties; corporate limited liability will not protect directors once criminal conduct and intentional concealment are proven.
